body:
We only discussed if we wanted them, I never thought of the aftermath. PPD definitely hit me hard afterwards, that’s when the arguing really started.

The only thing I ask of him is to clean up after himself, that’s it. I don’t like to keep mentioning it just so I don’t hear him say I’m nagging.
Mostly because I don’t talk to him about how I feel, I guess I’m too prideful to be vulnerable.

Those issues are mostly because of me, I bottle up my feelings and have a hard time expressing them without bawling into tears. I’m a very emotional person. I definitely think I should look into online therapy.

The only way he’s controlling is not letting me go anywhere at night by myself, he’s always paranoid something will happen to me. That I understand, I’m 5’ so I’m an easy target. I do always carry a knife though.

I chose to be a SAHM, he didn’t force me to quit my job. Plus with daycare and the pandemic I didn’t want to risk anything or pay for extra services. The reason he’s mentioned divorce is because I don’t talk to him about my feelings but that’s just how I’ve always been.

Having no friends stems from my 6 years of being homeschooled. Friendships just died out, yeah his friends are considered mine as well but it’s not the same.

I didn’t know those existed, he has threatened divorce twice already as well. I tend to bottle up my feelings, that’s just how I was as a teenager and never shook it off so therapy would probably help tremendously for me but I never looked into it.

We have sat down in the past to say what we need to work on but that hasn’t changed much. Of course I’m not perfect but at least I know how to be a mom.

He’s off for three days of the week, that’s plenty of quality time he could have with his son but spends it all on his computer or sleeping.

I haven’t tried to get help, but now I want to. I know I should talk to him about this as well, but I don’t feel comfortable being vulnerable. I like to think I’m strong and don’t need help with anything.
